onboarding.title: You are anonymous here
onboarding.explainer: Khabardar never asks for your name, phone number, or email. A random identity key is created on this device and never leaves it. Reports are anchored to a public blockchain as anonymous fingerprints — the content itself stays encrypted.
onboarding.createFailed: Your identity could not be created. Nothing was saved.
onboarding.phraseUnavailable: Your identity was created, but your 12 recovery words could not be read on this device. Open Settings → Recovery phrase and write them down before you rely on this device.
onboarding.writeTheseDown: Write these 12 words on paper before you continue. They are the only way back in if this device is lost or wiped. Nobody can recover them for you.
onboarding.iWroteThemDown: I have written these words down
onboarding.alreadyHavePhrase: I already have a recovery phrase

home.title: Reports
home.empty: No reports yet. Anything you compose stays encrypted on this device until you submit it.
home.karmaCheck: tap to check over this connection
home.networkUnprotected: This device is connecting directly. Your IP is visible to every server the app contacts.
home.storageUnreadable: This device's secure storage could not be read, so your identity cannot be loaded. On the web build this usually means the browser is blocking storage, for example private browsing or site data turned off.

compose.title: New report
compose.bodyPlaceholder: Describe the incident. Do not include your own name or details that identify you.
compose.entityHelp: This name stays on your device. Only a blinded tag is published, so other reports about the same office can be grouped with yours without naming it on the blockchain.
compose.locationPlaceholder: e.g. tsj9 — a 4-character geohash, city level only
compose.locationHelp: Only a coarse area code is recorded — never your precise location.
compose.evidenceNote: Metadata (EXIF, GPS, device info) is stripped and the file is encrypted before it is stored.
compose.visibilityPublicHelp: Anyone can read this report. Publish only what you are willing to have read by the public, including the people it names.
compose.visibilityJournalistsHelp: This build has no real journalist keys. The names on the list are samples. A report marked journalists-only is sealed to placeholder keys that no newsroom holds, so nobody intended can read it.
compose.recordingNote: Recording. The file is encrypted on this device and the plaintext copy is deleted.
compose.documentMetadataWarning: Documents are NOT re-encoded. Author names, revision history and tracked changes stay inside the file and can identify you. Consider photographing the page instead.
compose.audioWarning: A voice is biometric and identifies the speaker; background sound can reveal where you are. Record only if you accept both.
compose.evidenceTooLarge: That file is too large. The current limit is 8 MB per attachment.
compose.micDenied: Microphone permission is required to record audio evidence.

review.title: Review & submit
review.warning: Re-read your report. Remove anything that could identify you: names of colleagues only you work with, dates only you know, document numbers assigned to you.
review.hashNote: Only an encrypted fingerprint (hash) of this report goes on the blockchain. The report text and evidence never leave this device unencrypted.
review.gasNote: Submission is free — gas is sponsored. You do not need any cryptocurrency.
review.sponsoredBy: Gas for reports in this area is sponsored by %{name}.
review.journalistsDemoWarning: This report is marked journalists-only, but this build has no real journalist keys. Nobody at a newsroom can open it. Submit it only if you are testing the app.

status.title: Report status
status.draft: Draft — stored encrypted on this device
status.evidenceNote: Evidence is uploaded encrypted. These IDs point at ciphertext — useless without the report's content key.

settings.title: Settings
settings.panicExplainer: Immediately and permanently erases all drafts, evidence files, and your identity key from this device. On-chain fingerprints cannot be deleted, but nothing links them to this device once local data is gone.
settings.panicConfirmBody: This cannot be undone. All drafts, evidence, and your identity will be destroyed.
settings.otherExplainer: These are not part of anonymous reporting. An organization account is named and must never live on a device you report from.

moderation.title: Review queue
moderation.queueEmpty: Nothing in the queue. Submit a report to see it appear here.
moderation.readOnly: Act as a juror to vote on this report.

tips.title: Tip channel
tips.intro: Send an end-to-end encrypted message to a specific journalist or NGO. Unlike a report, a tip is never anchored on-chain — it is a private message, not a public record.
tips.transportWarning: A tip is sealed on this device and uploaded through the same transport as reports. On this build the upload stays on the device unless you configured a real content store. Start Tor on the Network screen before sending if the upload must not carry your IP.
tips.demoKeysWarning: The names on this list are samples. Their keys do not belong to any newsroom. A tip sealed to them cannot be opened by the organisation the name suggests.
tips.recipientKeyNote: Tips are sealed to this recipient's public key on your device. Nobody else — including the servers in between — can read them.
tips.messagePlaceholder: What do you want them to know? Leave out details that identify you unless you intend to be contacted.
tips.sealedStored: Tip sealed and uploaded. Only the recipient's key can open it. The upload used the current transport.
tips.sealedLocal: Tip sealed and kept on this device. Nothing left the phone. Configure a content store to actually deliver it.
tips.sealedOnly: Tip sealed, but storing it failed. Nothing readable was written anywhere.
tips.sentNote: Only a short preview and a digest are kept on this device. Panic delete removes these too.
tips.stub: End-to-end encrypted tip channel to journalists and NGOs.

feed.title: Public feed
feed.subtitle: Reports others chose to publish. Nothing here is proof — check the verification label before you believe it.
feed.empty: No reports match these filters yet.
feed.restrictedLong: The author restricted this report to verified journalists and NGOs. This device holds no key that can open it.
feed.unavailable: Content unavailable — the encrypted bundle could not be fetched.
feed.sampleNotice: This is a fictional sample report included so the feed is not empty. It describes no real person or incident.
feed.corroborateHelp: Only corroborate if you independently saw or experienced this. False corroboration destroys the signal that makes this feed useful.
feed.cannotCorroborateOwn: You cannot corroborate your own report.
feed.alreadyCorroborated: You have already corroborated this report.
feed.integrityOk: Content matches the on-chain fingerprint — it has not been altered since it was anchored.
feed.integrityFail: Content does NOT match the on-chain fingerprint. Treat this report as untrustworthy.
feed.integritySample: Not applicable — sample row, not anchored on-chain.

org.title: Organization workspace
org.separationWarning: This is a named, accountable account for newsrooms, NGOs, oversight bodies and funders. It is completely separate from anonymous reporting. If you also want to report something, do it from a different device or install — never from an account that identifies you.
org.accreditationNote: Until a human verifies your organization, only Community features are available. Analytics over a whistleblower corpus is not self-serve by design.
org.exportNote: Exports only reports you can already read. Restricted reports and reporter addresses are never included.
org.exportNotEntitled: Export requires an accredited Pro or Institutional plan.
org.devAccreditNote: Local development affordance: toggles accreditation so paid surfaces are explorable without a billing backend. Grants nothing on a real deployment.
org.poolsAttributionNote: Sponsors receive aggregate counts only. No sponsor is ever recorded against an individual report, because a narrow sponsor scope would shrink a reporter's anonymity set.
org.seatLimit: This plan has no seats left. Upgrade or revoke one first.
org.seatRevokeNote: Revoked seats are kept in the record, not deleted — who had access to this corpus and when is a question you will eventually have to answer.
org.apiNote: Only a hash is stored, so a stolen database yields no working credentials. A lost key cannot be recovered, only replaced.
org.apiKeyOnce: Copy this now — it is shown once and cannot be recovered.

wallet.title: Connect a wallet (optional)
wallet.intro: By default Khabardar signs your reports with a key created on this device, tied to nothing else. You can instead sign with your own wallet — but read the warning first.
wallet.warningBody: An external wallet usually has a history. If it has ever received funds, held an NFT, or been used on another site, that history can be connected to anything you submit here.
wallet.risk1: Exchange withdrawals link your wallet to a KYC identity.
wallet.risk2: Anyone can see every other transaction that wallet has made.
wallet.risk3: Reusing it elsewhere later can retroactively expose past reports.
wallet.recommendation: If your safety depends on staying anonymous, do not connect a wallet. Use the device key — it is the default for a reason.
wallet.connectedNote: Reports will be signed with this wallet until you disconnect.
wallet.scanUri: Scan this URI in your wallet, or copy it:
wallet.notConfigured: WalletConnect is not configured on this build. Set EXPO_PUBLIC_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID to enable it. The anonymous device key works without any configuration.
wallet.defaultNote: The device key remains the default. You never need a wallet to use Khabardar, and submissions are always gasless either way.

recovery.title: Recovery phrase
recovery.explainer: These 12 words are the only way to restore your identity and karma if you lose this device. Khabardar has no account and no password reset — nobody can recover this for you.
recovery.warning: Anyone who reads these words becomes you. Write them on paper. Do not screenshot them, and do not save them to a cloud notes app.
recovery.restoreExplainer: Enter your 12-word phrase to restore a previous identity on this device. This replaces the identity currently stored here.
recovery.restorePlaceholder: Enter your 12 words, separated by spaces
recovery.invalid: That phrase is not valid. Check the spelling and word order.

jury.intro: Reports are judged by a jury of equals voting in secret. Every juror counts exactly one — no weighting by reputation or anything else. Ballots are sealed until the panel is full, so nobody can see which way it is leaning while there is still time to join. Disagreeing costs a juror nothing.
jury.devModeNote: DEV ONLY: this toggle seats you as a juror locally. On a real deployment the contract decides who may vote and this grants nothing.
jury.commitPrompt: Choose a verdict. It is sealed — nobody sees it, including the other jurors, until the panel is full.
jury.revealPrompt: The panel is full. Open your ballot and say why.
jury.committed: Your ballot is sealed. Waiting for the rest of the panel.
jury.appealExplainer: You may contest this once. A larger panel re-hears it, and any credibility the verdict cost you is restored while it is reconsidered.
jury.reasonPlaceholder: Why? This reason is published with your vote.
jury.reasonNote: Your reason is published with your vote. Because the vote was sealed before you saw anyone else's, it cannot be rewritten to match the majority.
jury.simulateNote: DEMO ONLY: fabricates a panel so one device can reach quorum. Delete before any real deployment.
jury.auditNote: On a real deployment this is read from JuryVoteRevealed events, so the public can audit jurors with nothing but an RPC endpoint. Sealed ballots never appear — there is nothing in them to show.

rejected.already-committed: You have already sealed a ballot on this report.
rejected.not-committing: This report is not accepting ballots right now.
rejected.not-revealing: The panel is not full yet, so ballots cannot be opened.
rejected.already-revealed: You have already opened your ballot.
rejected.nothing-committed: You have no sealed ballot on this report.
rejected.self-review: You cannot judge your own report.
rejected.no-reason: A written reason is required to open a ballot.
rejected.no-salt: The key to your sealed ballot is missing from this device, so it cannot be opened.

queue.explainer: These could not be anchored, usually because there is no connection. They stay encrypted on this device and are retried when you open the app. Nothing is sent in the background.
queue.queuedNotice: Saved and queued. It will be retried next time you open the app, or tap Try sending now from the home screen.

stealth.title: Stealth
stealth.intro: These settings assume the person holding your phone is not you. They do not resist a forensic image taken before a wipe — they make a seized-and-unlocked phone survivable.
stealth.launcherLimit: A disguise can change the lock screen, and on Android the home-screen name and icon. It cannot change the package name. Settings and a listing of installed apps still show Khabardar.
stealth.launcherUnchanged: The lock-screen disguise is on. This build could not change the home-screen icon. On iOS that needs extra icon assets. On Android, rebuild the native project.
stealth.launcherResetFailed: The disguise is off. This build could not change the home-screen icon back, so it may still show the old name and icon.
stealth.lockExplainer: Require a PIN when the app opens.
stealth.duressExplainer: A second PIN that erases everything and then opens the app as if it were new. For when refusing to unlock is more dangerous than complying. The wipe is silent and cannot be undone.
stealth.disguiseExplainer: What the lock screen looks like, and on Android the home-screen name and icon. A recognisable anti-corruption app is itself evidence against its user.
stealth.captureExplainer: Prevents screenshots and hides the app-switcher preview. Both operating systems snapshot the current screen, and a snapshot of a report is the report.
stealth.pinTooSimple: That PIN is too easy to guess. Avoid repeated or sequential digits.
stealth.pinDuressMatchesReal: The duress PIN must be different from your unlock PIN.
stealth.lockUnreadable: The PIN could not be read, so the app cannot tell whether a lock is set. It has stayed locked rather than guess.

net.title: Network
net.direct: Direct — your IP is visible to every server this app contacts
net.proxied: Proxied — traffic is routed away from your IP
net.warning: No anonymising transport is wired in yet. Network metadata — which servers you contact and when — is currently the weakest part of this design, and it would identify a targeted user regardless of how good the encryption is.
net.requireExplainer: When on, any request that would go out without an anonymising transport fails instead of being sent. Nothing will work until a transport is configured — that is the point.
net.egressNote: Host names only, newest first. Kept on this device and erased by panic delete.
net.tor: Tor — traffic is onion-routed and the destination never sees your IP
net.claimedNotVerified: This transport claims to protect you but the app cannot confirm it. Trust it only as far as you trust whoever runs it.
net.torExplainer: Runs Tor inside the app and sends every request through it. Nothing is routed until you start it, and while it is running nothing falls back to a direct connection — a request that cannot go through Tor fails instead.
net.torBootstrapping: Connecting to the Tor network. This usually takes 10–60 seconds, and longer where Tor is blocked. Leave the app open.
net.torUnsupported: This build cannot run Tor. Expo Go and the web preview cannot load native code — you need a development build or a release binary. Until then this device connects directly.
net.bridgesExplainer: If the public Tor network is blocked, paste vanilla bridge lines here (an address, a port, a fingerprint). Get them from bridges.torproject.org. This build cannot run obfs4, snowflake or meek — those need a pluggable-transport binary we do not ship yet. Vanilla bridges help when directory authorities are blocked. They do not hide that the traffic is Tor from a network that is looking for it.
net.bridgesSaved: Saved %{count} bridge(s). Start Tor to use them.
net.bridgesCleared: No bridges saved. Tor will use the public network.
net.bridgesRestart: Saved. Stop Tor and start it again for the new bridges to take effect.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.notEntitled: Analytics requires an accredited Pro or Institutional plan.
analytics.privacyNote: Any group smaller than %{n} reports is withheld, not rounded. Small counts over a small area are a targeting tool, not a statistic — three reports in one district is enough for someone local to start guessing who filed them.
analytics.suppressed: %{buckets} group(s) covering %{reports} report(s) were withheld as too small to publish safely.
analytics.entityNote: Blinded tags, not names. Reports cluster without the accused office ever being published on-chain.
analytics.noData: Not enough data to show anything safely.

cases.title: Cases
cases.notEntitled: Case management requires an accredited Pro or Institutional plan.
cases.intro: Group related reports, track what was done, and record the outcome. Outcomes are the point: reports filed is an activity metric, investigations concluded is a result.
cases.noIdentifiersWarning: Never write anything about who a reporter might be. Notes are not protected the way reports are, and a case file that can answer 'is this the same person' is a deanonymization database.
cases.notePlaceholder: What did you do or find?
cases.closeReasonRequired: Closing a case requires a reason.
cases.actionRate: of concluded cases produced a real-world result

webDemo.title: This is a demonstration
webDemo.intro: You are looking at the web preview of Khabardar. It behaves like the real app and it does not protect you like the real app. Read this before you type anything into it.
webDemo.missingTitle: What is missing here that exists on a phone
webDemo.missingKeys: Your identity key and every encryption key are stored in this browser's localStorage, not in secure hardware. A browser extension, a malicious script, or anyone with access to this computer can read them.
webDemo.missingTor: There is no Tor. A browser cannot load the native module, so every request leaves from your real IP address.
webDemo.missingWipe: Panic delete cannot fully deliver. It clears this browser's storage, but the browser may already have copied those values into a profile, a sync, or a backup.
webDemo.doNotUse: Do not file a real report here. If you have something genuine to report, use a real build on a phone — or an established channel such as a newsroom's SecureDrop.
webDemo.whereReal: Everything you see is either sample data or stays on this device. Nothing is written to a blockchain and nothing is sent to a server.
webDemo.acknowledge: I understand — show me the demo
webDemo.footnote: No security audit has been performed on this project.

social.title: Profile
social.bioPlaceholder: Optional. Say as little as possible.
social.bioIdentifyingWarning: That bio names a job or a workplace. On a platform where reports are grouped by author, one detail like that plus a coarse area is often enough to identify someone. Consider removing it.
social.profileRiskNote: A profile groups reports by their author. That makes them easier to follow — and easier to pattern-match. Writing style, timing, and area across several reports can identify a person even though each report is anonymous. Use the hide control on anything sensitive.
social.listedExplainer: When off, this profile does not appear in search or suggestions.
social.followListExplainer: Off by default. Follower counts are harmless; the list of who you follow is a social graph, and a social graph over a reporting platform maps who trusts whom.
social.reactionsNote: Reactions are not evidence and never change a report's verification. Corroboration above is the evidentiary signal — this is not.
social.commentsWarning: Never speculate about who filed a report. If you see a comment doing it, report it — that reason hides the comment immediately.
social.commentPlaceholder: Add context, a correction, or a source.
social.followNothingYet: You are not following anything yet. Follow an accused office, an area, or a category from any report — those carry no reporter identity. Following a person does.

error.boundaryBody: The app hit an unexpected error and stopped drawing this screen. Your saved reports are untouched.
